pr_title: Custom data type history API usage in Python
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

Using the History API that returns lists instead of data frames with Python custom data types was having two issues: returning empty lists and timing out when enumerating the result in Python. 

These changes solve both issues by using the `Slice.Get(Type)` method instead of the generic `Slice.Get<T>()`, so that it can match the custom data in the slices to the actual Python class.

The timeout was being caused by a deadlock in the custom class readers data access, which is solved by wrapping Python custom data history requests results using `WrapPythonDataHistory`.

issue_context.title: Can't Make History Requests in Python for Custom/Alt Data Objects
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
In Python, like in C#, we can make a history request that returns data in our requested data type.
```
history = self.History[MyCustomDataType](self.symbol, 30, Resolution.Daily)
```

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
In C#, we have no issues.

In Python, we can request a DataFrame. If we request the data be in our a list of the data type, when we try to iterate through the result, the algorithm just times out.
```
history = self.History[MyCustomDataType](self.symbol, 30, Resolution.Daily)
# This line just causes a time-out:
[x for x in history]
```
> Algorithm.Initialize() Error: Execution Security Error: Operation timed out - 5 minutes max. Check for recursive loops. Stack Trace: Execution Security Error: Operation timed out - 5 minutes max. Check for recursive loops.


#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
N/A

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->
Python: https://www.quantconnect.com/terminal/processCache?request=embedded_backtest_b004df9c56245296dc6dfbf4897d1598.html

C#: https://www.quantconnect.com/terminal/processCache?request=embedded_backtest_86cec936cde21ef37da9eee228301674.html
